case.question: Is there a tennis program for people who are blind or have low vision?

result.answer:
Yes. The publisher, AAA Play, writes that the Blind Tennis Program is run by Blind Sports & Recreation Victoria, Tennis Victoria and Tennis Seniors Victoria.

For adults, it runs as a six-week program during school terms on Friday nights on indoor courts at the National Tennis Centre. Players use various balls, including audible tennis balls and different sized and coloured balls, with help from volunteers. A junior version is open to kids aged 5 to 15 who are blind or have vision problems, with junior programs also at Lalor, Keilor, Williamstown and Cheltenham.

The publisher lists $80 per year, $5 per occasional session, and $20 per term for juniors. Details: https://aaaplay.org.au/activity/blind-tennis-program/

case.question: Is there a playground with Braille and Auslan signs that kids in wheelchairs can use?

result.answer:
Yes — one match in the published programs here.

The publisher, AAA Play, writes that Brimbank Park Playscape "is a fun place for kids and families to enjoy nature. All kids can play here, even those in wheelchairs. You can find Braille and Auslan signs, fun wall paintings, a build-your-own playhouse, and more." They suggest checking the Maribyrnong Valley Parklands page for news before you go.

Details: https://aaaplay.org.au/activity/brimbank-park-playscape/ (page: /events/DS-09:activity:20854)

That is the publisher's own description, not a checked access audit — nothing else is published here about it.

case.question: Do any of the Reclink footy programs provide transport?

result.answer:
Yes — the publisher, AAA Play, writes for each Reclink Footy team that "transport provided for away games", along with lunch and equipment.

Three of them, with their home grounds as written:
- Sunbury Phoenix — home games in Sunbury (/events/DS-09:activity:22538)
- Salvo Hawks — home games in Hawthorn (/events/DS-09:activity:22472)
- Southern Peninsula Swans — home games at Olympic Park Recreational Reserve, 90 Besgrove St, Rosebud (/events/DS-09:activity:22503)

One more, the Cardinia Tigers (Bunyip), is in the same list. The publisher does not describe transport to home games, so check that with the Reclink Footy manager.

case.question: Is there a unified football program for young people with disability run with Melbourne Victory?

result.answer:
Yes. The publisher, AAA Play, writes that the "Melbourne Victory All Abilities Unified Football Program" is "for young people with disability or additional support needs", offering "a fun, safe, and welcoming place to play football, learn new skills, make friends, and have fun."

They list four sessions:
- Ages 16+, 11:00am–12:00pm, bi-weekly, 14 October – 16 December (/events/DS-09:activity:25160)
- Ages 6–16 and 12–18, 10:30am–11:20am, 17 October – 5 December (/events/DS-09:activity:25162)
- Ages 6–16 and 16+, 5:00pm–5:50pm, 16 October – 4 December (/events/DS-09:activity:25161)
- A Melbourne Victory All Abilities Football Centre in Fawkner (/events/DS-09:activity:25033)

case.question: Does any program description say the exact start time of the Blind Tennis Program?
case.note: The description does state 6:30 pm; the answer must attribute it to the publisher.

result.answer:
Yes. The publisher, AAA Play, writes that the adults program runs "Friday evenings from 6:30 pm to 8:00 pm", and the juniors program "Friday evenings from 5:30 pm to 6:30 pm", during school terms.

They also note the last program for the year runs from October 11th to December 13th, at the National Tennis Centre on indoor courts.

Source: https://aaaplay.org.au/activity/blind-tennis-program/ (page: /events/DS-09:activity:20905)
